newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK minorities face wait past June for UK passports.
newsitem.headline: HK minorities face wait past June for UK passports.

text.p: Hong Kong's ethnic minority residents entitled to British passports may not receive them until after the territory's handover to China, a senior British official said on Tuesday.
Francis Cornish, Britain's senior Trade Commisioner in Hong Kong, told reporters it was difficult to say when the process would start or when the first passport would be issued.
"It will mostly take place after the handover," he said.
Hong Kong reverts to China on July 1 after 150 years of British colonial rule.

"We are likely to start the process of registering applicants before the handover, but it is a big operation...how long it takes will depend on the number of applicants we get, but we're talking about thousands certainly," he said.

London announced in February it would grant full British passports to up to 8,000 ethnic minority Hong Kong residents, mostly of South Asian origin, who faced the prospect of becoming stateless when China resumes sovereignty over the colony.
While they will still have residency rights after the handover, as non-Chinese it was unclear whether they would be entitled to passports of the future Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
